subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the absolute maximum value and the absolute minimum value of the function f(x) = x + sin 2x in [0, π].

mark_split.label: Differentiate and set the derivative to zero
Find every critical point inside the interval
Evaluate f at the critical points and at both endpoints
Compare the values and state both extrema

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which points you must evaluate the function at on a closed interval, and say whether the second derivative test is needed here.

steps.label: Differentiate and set the derivative to zero
steps.margin_note: First mark. State that f is continuous on the closed interval — that is what guarantees an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum exist. The chain rule gives the factor 2 in 2cos 2x.
lines: f(x) = x + sin 2x on the closed interval [0, π].
f is continuous on [0, π] and differentiable on (0, π), so an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum both exist on this interval.

recall.must_convey: That f′(x) = 1 + 2cos 2x, and that critical points come from f′(x) = 0.
accept: differentiate x plus sin two x
the derivative is one plus two cos two x
the chain rule gives the extra two
sin two x differentiate cheste two cos two x vasthundi
set the first derivative equal to zero
f is continuous on the closed interval so both extrema exist
heard_as: one plus two cos two x

steps.why: An absolute extremum on a closed interval sits either at a point where the derivative is zero or at an endpoint. Differentiating is how the first group is found.
common_mistakes: Writing f′(x) = 1 + cos 2x and dropping the chain rule factor 2.
steps.memory_tip: The derivative of sin 2x carries the inside derivative out in front: 2cos 2x. The 2 is the chain rule showing itself.

steps.label: Find every critical point inside the interval
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Convert the range for x into a range for 2x first. Missing the second solution 4π/3 is the usual slip here.
lines: x lies in [0, π], so 2x lies in [0, 2π].
In [0, 2π] the equation cos 2x = −1/2 has the solutions
∴ x = π/3  and  x = 2π/3 are the critical points, and both lie in [0, π].

recall.must_convey: That cos 2x = −1/2 with 2x in [0, 2π] gives 2x = 2π/3 and 4π/3, so x = π/3 and x = 2π/3.
accept: cos two x equals minus half
two x lies between zero and two pi
the solutions are two pi by three and four pi by three
x range ni two x range ga marchali
the critical points are pi by three and two pi by three
cosine is negative in the second and third quadrants

steps.why: Doubling the variable doubles the range, so [0, π] for x becomes [0, 2π] for 2x. Working in the 2x range is what shows there are two solutions here rather than one.
common_mistakes: Solving cos x = −1/2 instead of cos 2x = −1/2, giving x = 2π/3 alone.
steps.memory_tip: Solve for the whole angle 2x first, over its own doubled range, and divide by 2 only at the end.

steps.label: Evaluate f at the critical points and at both endpoints
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Both endpoints must appear in the list. Leaving out f(0) and f(π) is the classic error on this type, and here it changes both answers.
lines: For an absolute extremum on a closed interval, evaluate f at every critical point AND at both endpoints.

recall.must_convey: That f is evaluated at x = 0, π/3, 2π/3 and π, giving 0, π/3 + √3/2, 2π/3 − √3/2 and π.
accept: evaluate at the critical points and at both endpoints
f of zero is zero and f of pi is pi
sin four pi by three is minus root three by two
rendu endpoints kooda check cheyyali
make a list of four values
f of pi by three is pi by three plus root three by two

steps.why: An absolute extremum on a closed interval is not the same as a local one. The largest and smallest values can sit at an endpoint, where the derivative need not be zero at all, so the endpoints must be tested.
common_mistakes: Testing only the critical points and never the endpoints.
steps.memory_tip: On a closed interval the answer list always has two more entries than there are critical points — one for each endpoint.

steps.label: Compare the values and state both extrema
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Both extrema here sit at the endpoints. A student who compared only the two critical values would answer 1.9132 and 1.2284, and both would be wrong.
lines: The largest is π, reached at x = π.
The smallest is 0, reached at x = 0.
Both extreme values occur at the ENDPOINTS, not at either critical point.

lines.text: ∴ absolute maximum = π at x = π,  and absolute minimum = 0 at x = 0

recall.must_convey: That the largest of the four values is π at x = π and the smallest is 0 at x = 0.
accept: the absolute maximum is pi at x equal to pi
the absolute minimum is zero at x equal to zero
compare all four values and pick the largest and smallest
rendu answers endpoints daggara vasthayi
both extreme values are at the endpoints here
the critical points give neither the largest nor the smallest value

steps.why: The absolute extrema are simply the largest and smallest members of the list. No second derivative test is needed on a closed interval — comparing the values is the complete method.
common_mistakes: Applying the second derivative test and reporting a local extremum as the absolute one.
Giving the x values instead of the function values as the maximum and minimum.
steps.memory_tip: Absolute extrema on a closed interval are found by comparing a LIST, not by a sign test. Build the list, then read off the largest and the smallest.

insider_note: Absolute extrema on a CLOSED interval need the endpoints tested as well as the stationary points — the largest may sit at x = π. Compare all the values at the end rather than using a second-derivative test.
